searchText: I had trouble getting Sepolia peers with a fresh Geth instance, and someone else in the Lighthouse Discord noticed the same. Are Geth's bootnodes up-to-date for Sepolia? There are only two sepolia bootnodes, one geth. Both are online but have too many peers. Peering should just work over the dht and the dns list, just not that many nodes on there Hi, what does the EL do if I send twice the same FCU with the same payload attributes for the next slot, does it restart block production or does it ignore the second call? Is there any penalty in calling twice? If the attributes are exactly the same, we don't start a new task. If you change them up a bit, we will start a new building task Having two tasks building at the same time costs cpu <@755590043632140352> Thanks a lot Marius, I was hoping for this, hopefully other ELs do something similar There are a few edge cases where I sort of can't avoid calling twice with the same attributes When do we expect releases from client teams with the goerli shapella fork built in? We have ~7 days to the fork and would need to also give users some time to upgrade we had to delay our release for a couple of days due to a regression, soaking now and expecting to release tomorrow/thursday if no new issues appear Releasing today/tomorrow I think it probably makes sense for the post to go out tomorrow, even if some clients are missing (we can mark them `TBD`) so people can know it's happening and to expect releases soon > This value MUST be either equal to or an ancestor of headBlockHash This also applies to `finalizedBlockHash` - right? (not sure if this is the correct channel to ask this BTW) Yes, we return INVALID if the final block is not an ancestor of head. (this is the correct channel for this imo) I assumed so, great 🙂 How does Geth/other clients perform this check? I do not want to scan the entire chain to see if this condition is met hmm, I think EL should return an error, not invalid in this case This is part of the hive tests we will release today 🙂 ```go // If the finalized block is not in our canonical tree, somethings wrong finalBlock := api.eth.BlockChain().GetBlockByHash(update.FinalizedBlockHash) if finalBlock == nil { log.Warn("Final block not available in database", "hash", update.FinalizedBlockHash) return engine.STATUS_INVALID, engine.InvalidForkChoiceState.With(errors.New("final block not available in database")) } else if rawdb.ReadCanonicalHash(api.eth.ChainDb(), finalBlock.NumberU64()) != update.FinalizedBlockHash { log.Warn("Final block not in canonical chain", "number", block.NumberU64(), "hash", update.HeadBlockHash) return engine.STATUS_INVALID, engine.InvalidForkChoiceState.With(errors.New("final block not in canonical chain")) } ``` Oh we return an error, not invalid ``` engine-api/Inconsistent Head in Fork engine-api/Inconsistent Safe in Fork engine-api/Inconsistent Finalized in Fork ``` yeah, we're working in the same way 😉 Oh right this is the obvious way to do this check 🤦‍♂️ Need more coffee We're up to 5/9 of clients released, so I think we should go ahead and put out the blog post tomorrow (morning PT), and then add other releases as they go out. Otherwise, assuming we changed the fork time, we'd need to re-release more than half of clients. testnet deprecation notice, yell if you need it around for something 😄

excerpts.author: sproul
excerpts.content: I had trouble getting Sepolia peers with a fresh Geth instance, and someone else in the Lighthouse Discord noticed the same. Are Geth's bootnodes up-to-date for Sepolia?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: There are only two sepolia bootnodes, one geth. Both are online but have too many peers. Peering should just work over the dht and the dns list, just not that many nodes on there

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Hi, what does the EL do if I send twice the same FCU with the same payload attributes for the next slot, does it restart block production or does it ignore the second call? Is there any penalty in calling twice?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: If the attributes are exactly the same, we don't start a new task. If you change them up a bit, we will start a new building task

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Having two tasks building at the same time costs cpu

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Thanks a lot Marius, I was hoping for this, hopefully other ELs do something similar

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: There are a few edge cases where I sort of can't avoid calling twice with the same attributes
